headline: COP31 draft cover decision sets first-ever 2035 CCUS and carbon-removal capacity goals
summary: The Türkiye COP31 Presidency's first draft cover decision proposes, for the first time in a COP text, quantified scale-up goals for carbon management — at least ~500 Mt CO₂/yr of CCUS capacity by 2035, alongside a longer-term ambition cited at 1.3–2.5 Gt/yr. The Presidency stressed the draft reflects divergent national positions, not consensus, and EU climate chief Wopke Hoekstra dismissed it as a “shopping list” at odds with the logic of implementation; adoption is targeted for the closing plenary on Friday.
co2crc_note: First COP cover text to quantify global CCUS deployment ambition — a material policy signal for CCS investment and for Australia's international positioning.
extractor_note: Capacity figure is a draft policy target (not consensus); a longer-term 1.3–2.5 Gt/yr ambition is also cited. Page-level date confirmed via Google Alerts feed ISO timestamp + web search corroboration (WebFetch blocked for carbonherald.com this session).

headline: CNPC commissions what it calls China's longest CO₂ pipeline for Jilin CCUS-EOR
summary: PetroChina/CNPC has put into operation a long-distance dense-phase CO₂ pipeline feeding its Jilin oilfield CCUS-EOR complex in the Songliao Basin, north-east China. The first phase runs about 282 km with a design capacity of roughly 3.3 Mt CO₂/yr (the planned full route is near 400 km linking Changchun, Jilin, Songyuan and Siping), extending CNPC's commercial CCUS-EOR push — the company has cumulatively injected more than 13 Mt CO₂.
co2crc_note: An Asian NOC scaling CO₂ transport infrastructure — a benchmark for dense-phase pipeline and CCUS-EOR deployment relevant to APAC transport value chains.
extractor_note: 'Longest' is CNPC's own, historically contested claim; first-phase length/capacity from corroborating background search. Capacity_mtpa is a transport figure (not additive to capture). Date via alerts feed + two outlets (WebFetch blocked).

headline: Plans to rely on carbon removal and CCS at COP31 spark scientific debate
summary: New Scientist reports growing contention at COP31 over the draft cover decision's heavy reliance on carbon dioxide removal and CCS to manage the 1.5°C overshoot, with scientists and campaigners warning the technologies remain unproven at the scale implied and risk diluting near-term emission cuts.
co2crc_note: Signals social-licence and credibility risk around over-reliance on CDR/CCS in global climate policy — relevant to how CCS is framed publicly.

headline: COP31 ‘Think Negative’ pavilion draws strong crowds as carbon removal takes centre stage
summary: Carbon Herald reports the dedicated carbon-removal pavilion at COP31 drew large crowds, reflecting the rising mainstream profile of CDR — including DAC and BECCS — within the UN climate negotiations.
co2crc_note: Indicator of growing visibility and engagement for carbon removal at COP — a positive momentum signal for the CDR/CCS sector.
